title: Waiting-Period Anchor for Deductible Decreases on Loan Transactions — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
## NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own): dating a deductible decrease recorded for a loan transaction

For a pending deductible decrease recorded for a loan transaction on a tier that carries no ICC coverage, the anchor rule gives the date the waiting period runs from:

| Situation on the records | The change is dated from |
|---|---|
| The request records a loan closing date and the premium was received no later than that date | The loan closing date |
| The change was requested with the coming term's renewal premium | The coming term start |
| Otherwise | The receipt date |

The lines are read in order and the first that holds gives the anchor. "Received no later than that date" means the latest premium payment on the policy received on or after the request date is posted on or before the loan closing date recorded on the request; a payment on the closing day itself qualifies. "Requested with the coming term's renewal premium" means a premium payment for the coming term — the term starting on the current term end — is posted on or after the request date. The receipt date is the later of the request date and the date of the latest premium payment on the policy received on or after the request date.

*Hypothetical cases.* A request records a closing date ten days after the request date and the premium is posted five days after the request date: the change is dated from the loan closing date. The same request with the premium posted one day after the closing date: the first line fails, and absent a payment for the coming term the change is dated from the receipt date.
